subject: accountancy

concepts.title: Bank Reconciliation Statement Overview
concepts.definition: A schedule compiled periodically to reconcile discrepancies between the cash book bank column balance and the bank passbook balance.
concepts.formula: Cash Book Balance + Adjustments = Passbook Balance
concepts.key_idea: Identifies and explains variations between firm records and bank records as of a given date.
question_patterns: what is a bank reconciliation statement
why is a bank reconciliation statement prepared
state the purpose of preparing bank reconciliation statement
explain the need for bank reconciliation
explain bank reconciliation statement overview

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether reconciliation starts from cash book balance or passbook balance.
Cross-check debit and credit entries between cash book and bank passbook to find mismatched items.
List timing differences and errors that cause the variance between both records.

concepts.title: Reconciliation from Favourable Cash Book Balance
concepts.definition: Ascertaining the bank passbook balance starting from a positive debit balance shown in the cash book.
concepts.formula: passbook_balance = cash_book_balance + cheques_issued_unpresented + direct_credits - cheques_deposited_uncleared - direct_debits
concepts.key_idea: Add items that increase passbook balance relative to cash book and deduct items that decrease it.

find balance as per passbook starting from cash book debit balance

solution_steps.explain: Sum up unpresented cheques issued and direct bank credits like interest or dividends.
Sum up uncleared deposited cheques and direct bank debits like bank charges.
Add total additions to cash book balance and subtract total deductions.

concepts.title: Reconciliation from Favourable Pass Book Balance
concepts.definition: Determining the cash book balance starting from a positive credit balance in the bank passbook.
concepts.formula: cash_book_balance = passbook_balance + cheques_deposited_uncleared + direct_debits - cheques_issued_unpresented - direct_credits
concepts.key_idea: Reverse the treatment used when starting from cash book balance.
question_patterns: calculate cash book balance given passbook credit balance
find balance as per cash book starting from passbook balance
compute cash book balance from passbook balance
prepare bank reconciliation statement starting with passbook balance
calculate reconciliation from favourable pass book balance for the given values

solution_steps.explain: Sum up uncleared deposited cheques and direct debits made by the bank.
Sum up unpresented cheques issued and direct credits collected by the bank.
Add total additions to passbook balance and subtract total deductions.

concepts.title: Reconciliation from Cash Book Overdraft Balance
concepts.definition: Calculating passbook overdraft balance starting from a credit (unfavourable) balance in the cash book.
concepts.formula: passbook_overdraft = cash_book_overdraft + cheques_deposited_uncleared + direct_debits - cheques_issued_unpresented - direct_credits
concepts.key_idea: Items increasing bank draft/liability are added while items reducing overdraft are deducted.

concepts.definition: Calculating cash book balance or overdraft starting from a debit (unfavourable) balance in the passbook.

concepts.title: Timing Differences in Bank Transactions
concepts.definition: Variances caused by the difference in time of entering a transaction in the firm's cash book versus bank's ledger.
concepts.key_idea: Discrepancies arise naturally due to processing delay for cheques clearing, direct deposits, or standing instructions.
question_patterns: identify timing differences between cash book and passbook
state causes of difference due to time gap
explain why unpresented cheques cause difference in balance
what are time lag differences in bank reconciliation
explain timing differences in bank transactions

solution_steps.explain: Check if transaction was recorded in one book but delayed in another due to clearance or notification gap.
Determine if it relates to uncollected cheques, unpresented cheques, direct collections, or standing orders.

concepts.title: Errors in Cash Book and Bank Pass Book
concepts.definition: Inconsistencies resulting from incorrect recording, omission, or casting errors made by the firm or the bank.
concepts.key_idea: Clerical mistakes in recording numbers or sides in cash book/passbook lead to balance differences.
question_patterns: identify errors committed by firm or bank

solution_steps.explain: Find whether the wrong entry, double entry, or casting error occurred in the cash book or passbook.
Determine if the error inflated or deflated the cash book or passbook balance relative to the correct figure.

questions: From the following particulars, prepare a bank reconciliation statement as at March 31, 2017: (i) Balance as per cash book Rs 3,200 (ii) Cheque issued but not presented for payment Rs 1,800 (iii) Cheque deposited but not collected upto March 31, 2017 Rs 2,000 (iv) Bank charges debited by bank Rs 150.

On March 31, 2017 the cash book showed a balance of Rs 3,700 as cash at bank, but the bank passbook made up to same date showed that cheques for Rs 700, Rs 300 and Rs 180 respectively had not presented for payment, Also, a cheque amounting to Rs 1,200 deposited into the account had not been credited. Prepare a bank reconciliation statement.

The cash book shows a bank balance of Rs 7,800. Discrepancies: (a) Cheque deposited in bank but not credited Rs 3,000 (b) Cheque issued but not yet present for payment Rs 1,500 (c) Insurance premium paid by the bank Rs 2,000 (d) Bank interest credit by the bank Rs 400 (e) Bank charges Rs 100 (f) Directly deposited by a customer Rs 4,000. Prepare BRS.

Bank balance of Rs 40,000 showed by cash book of Atul on December 31, 2016. Cheques of Rs 2,000, Rs 5,000 and Rs 8,000 deposited were not credited till January 02, 2017. Cheques of Rs 7,000 and Rs 8,000 issued were not presented till January 03, 2017. Bank credited Rs 325 as interest and debited Rs 50 for bank charges not in cash book. Prepare BRS.

Cash book bank balance Rs 40,960 on March 31, 2017. Items: (a) Bank charges Rs 100 not in cash book. (b) Debtor paid Rs 2,000 directly to bank not in cash book. (c) Cheques totaling Rs 12,980 issued not presented. (d) Bill for Rs 6,900 discounted entered in cash book without discount charge of Rs 800. (e) Rs 3,520 deposited not credited. (f) Dishonour of cheque Rs 650 not in cash book. Prepare BRS.

Prepare BRS on Dec 31, 2017. Passbook balance Rs 7,000. (a) Cheque Rs 1,000 directly deposited by customer. (b) Bank credited Rs 700 interest. (c) Out of Rs 3,000 cheques issued, Rs 1,000 not presented. Find cash book balance.

Prepare BRS showing balance as per cash book on Dec 31, 2016. Passbook balance Rs 50,000. (a) Cheques Rs 2,000 and Rs 5,000 paid in October not credited till Dec. (b) Cheque Rs 800 entered in cash book omitted to be banked. (c) Cheques Rs 10,000 issued in Nov not credited. (d) Interest on investment Rs 1,000 collected by bank.

Passbook balance of Mr. Kumar Rs 3,000. (a) Cheques paid in not cleared: Ram Kumar Rs 1,000, Kishore Kumar Rs 500. (b) Bank charges Rs 300. (c) Cheques issued not presented: Hameed Rs 2,000, Kapoor Rs 500. (d) Interest in passbook not in cash book Rs 100. Prepare BRS.

On Jan 1, 2017, Rakesh had overdraft Rs 8,000 in cash book. Cheques Rs 2,000 paid in not collected. Issued cheques Rs 800 not presented. Passbook debit of Rs 60 interest and Rs 100 bank charges. Prepare BRS.
